Like Yeri, Agi shows regular penultimate stress and cognates like anóra 'descend' fit the typical stress pattern. The loss of word-final /a/ in positions preceded by sonorants is a possible historical explanation for this uncommon stress pattern in Yeri.[fn 29] Several Yeri words which show word-final stress and their Agi cognates, which were recorded while in the field, are presented in Table 2.3…
new_statements.rule_in_words: Primary stress falls regularly on the penultimate syllable of the word (Wilson's five field-recorded Agi forms in Table 2.31 are all penult-stressed: [anÓra] 'descend', [hanÓla] 'tree grub', [hapára] 'overripe coconut', [bianára] 'piane tree', [lombála] 'mushroom'). Competing older statement: Laycock 1968 (survey wordlists, article-wide convention) writes stress only when it is NOT on the first syllable not containing schwa and says 'Stress does not appear to be a phonemic feature in any of these languages'; his 41-item Agi list has one accent-marked form (omóniya 'bad', 2nd of 4 syllables) and 40 unmarked. The two agree for disyllables and schwa-initial words but not for longer words; Wilson's trained-linguist field statement is preferred.
new_statements.secondary_stress: Nothing said for Agi (Wilson's 'secondary stress on alternate syllables preceding the main stress' is stated for Yeri only, p. 73).
new_statements.exceptions: None for Agi; the passage is precisely about Agi lacking the Yeri exception (final stress in some disyllables) because Agi keeps a word-final /a/ that Yeri lost after sonorants.
new_statements.domain_note: Word-level, isolated lexical items (cognate list); no statement about phrase-level or citation-form effects. Laycock 1968 adds the survey-wide claim that stress is not phonemic in any of the Lumi-area languages, Agi included.
new_statements.identity_note: No description of Agi itself exists. The deciding statement is a comparative remark inside Wilson's grammar of the sister language Yeri (yapu1240), based on Wilson's own Agi field recordings made near Yeri village; the Agi she recorded is the variety of the Yolpa/Boni/Wuro villages, and she notes (p. 6) that Wuro Agi is closer to Yeri than the Agi of the other villages. Laycock 1968 lists Agi as language no. 19 (villages Boini, Ori, Wuro, Yuolpa; informants Salawan and Masaru of Wuro; alt. name Ori) and Laycock 1973 as entry 32 'AGI (Metru)'. Same glottocode agii1245 throughout.
